title: Mausi Meets No One
logline: Kiran gives Mausi the all-clear with the groom wide awake beside her, then tells him what the other answer would have done. They drive to the bureau at dawn as two thieves who married each other, and inside Mausi, delighted with her new son-in-law, takes Kiran's left wrist to strip the chooda for tomorrow's bride, an arm's length from the man hunting the scar beneath it.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut. Hindi terms of address and named objects kept as spoken in India: Mausi, beta, meri bachchi, Damaad ji, Jijaji, saale sahab, Didi, chooda, mathri.
script_note: Indian English in Latin script; spoken text equals subtitle text with the square-bracket tags removed.

characters.name: Kiran
characters.role: LEAD. The bureau's vanishing bride; tonight 'Sneha'. She has just given the all-clear with the groom awake.
characters.look: Indian woman, 27, about 5 ft 3, slight and wiry. Wheat-brown skin, oval face, straight dark brows, large kajal-lined eyes, closed watchful mouth. Low bun, centre parting with sindoor, two loose strands at the temples, small round red bindi, thin plain gold ring in the LEFT nostril, small gold studs, short black-bead mangalsutra. Block henna on both hands (solid disc in each palm, fingertips dipped). Red-and-ivory chooda on both forearms: a red cuff about 10 cm long with a pale ivory band at each end, starting just above the wrist bone. b1 to b3: plain sindoor-red matte saree with a thin plain gold border, red elbow-sleeved blouse, barefoot. From b5: plain ash-grey cotton salwar-kurta, three-quarter sleeves ending a hand's width above the chooda, grey dupatta over the left shoulder, flat black sandals. The scar on the LEFT outer forearm stays under the cuff in every shot.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, late 20s, alto with a dry edge. Small-city Madhya Pradesh Indian English, learnt at school and from a phone: simple, quick, contractions. Not British, not American. In this episode she is Kiran, not 'Sneha': lower, flat, quick, short sentences to Aditya. With Mausi she sounds younger and softer, and ends on 'Mausi'. Under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never shrill. Lies come easily; true things come after a pause (l05).

characters.name: Aditya
characters.role: The groom, a pharmacist, Mohit's elder brother. From b6 he plays a greedy thief who married a thief.
characters.look: Indian man, 33, about 6 ft, tall and narrow, slight stoop. Light-brown skin, long clean-shaven face, high forehead, calm deep-set eyes, thin mouth, short neat black hair parted on his left. Rimless rectangular glasses in every shot. Plain cream cotton-silk wedding kurta with band collar, sleeves folded back once, side pocket on the right; cream churidar. A 5 cm brass key on a doubled red cotton thread worn outside the kurta at mid-chest, in every shot. Plain steel watch, brown strap, left wrist. Barefoot in the bedroom, tan sandals outside.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, early 30s, light baritone, soft-spoken. Careful small-city Madhya Pradesh Indian English, a science graduate's: complete sentences, precise nouns (dose, medical store, sachet), no slang. Not British, not American. Even and unhurried. Calls Billu 'saale sahab' only while playing the greedy husband (l11). Playing the greedy husband (l11, l14, l15) he lets a little amusement in, but he never raises his voice and never swears.

characters.name: Shakun Mausi
characters.role: Runs the brides. Voice on a phone in b1 and b7; seen for the first time in this series in b9.
characters.look: Indian woman, 56, about 5 ft 2, broad and heavy-shouldered. Brown skin, round face, heavy-lidded shrewd eyes, paan-reddened lips, large round maroon bindi, small gold nose stud, grey-streaked black hair oiled into a tight bun. Starched bottle-green cotton saree with a narrow mustard border, mustard elbow-sleeved blouse, thin gold chain, rubber slippers. A steel ring of about eight keys hooked at her LEFT hip. A dozen plain green glass bangles on each wrist; forearms otherwise bare and unmarked.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, mid 50s, low, warm, grainy, a paan-chewer's unhurried mouth. Warm, motherly Bundelkhand-side Indian English with a strong Hindi accent, short plain sentences; she sounds like someone's aunt at a wedding. Not British, not American. Hindi endearments kept (beta, meri bachchi, Damaad ji), one in every second line. Laughs easily. On the phone she is fully voiced and clear, never a whisper. The colder the decision, the softer and slower (l19).

characters.name: Billu
characters.look: Indian man, 30, about 5 ft 7, wiry and restless. Brown skin, sharp jaw, patchy stubble, black hair gelled straight back. Faded blue denim jacket with sleeves pushed up over a black round-neck T-shirt, dark jeans, white sneakers gone grey. Wooden toothpick in the right corner of his mouth; car key on a plain steel ring hooked on his right index finger, except while driving (b7 to b9), when it is in the ignition. No weapon.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, about 30, light tenor, fast, a little nasal, talks round a toothpick. Quick, slangy small-town Bundelkhand Indian English with a heavy Hindi accent, an article dropped now and then; keeps Jijaji, Mausi, arre. Never American street slang, not British. Cocky and joking when he thinks he is in charge; goes loud for one line when surprised (l09), then looks to Mausi.

characters.name: Chhoti
characters.role: The next bride in training. Her first wedding is tomorrow (day 3). An adult woman.
characters.look: Adult woman, 19, about 5 ft 1, slight, light-brown skin, wide curious eyes. One long black braid over her right shoulder. Plain mustard-yellow cotton kurta with short sleeves, white salwar, a plain dupatta, rubber slippers. Two thin green glass bangles on the right wrist; left wrist bare; both forearms plainly unmarked. A phone in a plain pink cover in her right hand. Henna half done in Kiran's block style: LEFT palm disc and fingertips done, RIGHT hand bare. Nothing about her reads as a child (D-007 direction 14).
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, 19, a young woman's voice, not a child's: bright, quick, a giggle in the breath. Light, eager small-town Indian English in short sentences. Not British, not American. Calls Kiran Didi.

characters.name: The boys
characters.role: Billu's two helpers. Silent. Seen only in b2 and not again in this branch.
characters.look: Never a face. Two backlit shapes from behind on a motorbike: one heavy-set, shaved head, maroon track jacket; one thin, checked shirt, cloth cap. Heads turned away or in shadow.

location: Five places, one night into one dawn: the bridal bedroom of the rented house (b1, b3, b5); the empty lane below with Billu's white sedan under one sodium streetlight (b2); the narrow stairwell and front door (b6); Billu's car on an empty highway at dawn, then stopped at a grey steel shutter (b7 to b9); the front room of Shubh Lagan Marriage Bureau and Beauty Parlour, shut to customers, shutter up, daylight and tube light (b10, b11). No crowd anywhere; no readable text in any image.
time_of_day: Night 1, 2:00 am (b1 to b5) and 3:00 am (b6); day 2 dawn, about 5:00 to 5:40 am (b7 to b9); day 2 early morning, about 5:45 am (b10, b11).

beats.action: Opens inside the same breath that ended s1e02. Shot 1 (l01): extreme close-up of Kiran's mouth and lower face in the amber lamplight, red saree, the pallu fallen over her LEFT forearm (picture-right when she faces camera); the cuff is complete again. Shot 2 (l02): insert of her black phone in its plain dark-red cover face-up on the white sheet between them, on speaker, caller name 'Mausi' (overlay; 'मौसी' in the Hindi cut) and 2:00 as overlays, a marigold petal on the sheet beside it. Silent after: two-shot across the bed, a room's width apart, the untouched steel glass on the stool between them, the steel dabba still in Aditya's hand. The call-ended tone; Aditya, glasses on, key on its red thread, lets out a breath and lowers his eyes: the check he expected, the answer he expected.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Yes, Mausi. He drank it.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [chuckles] Well done, meri bachchi. Billu will be downstairs at three.

beats.action: One still, no line. Billu leans on the bonnet of the white sedan under the sodium streetlight, toothpick in, pocketing his phone with his right hand, the car key hooked on his index finger. Behind him, deeper in the empty lane, the two boys are backlit shapes from behind on the motorbike, heads turned away, its red tail light already moving off. The bike's engine kicks and recedes (sound). Billu is the only face.

Same room, same night. Shot 1 (l03): Kiran single, sitting on the bed's window side, her voice dropped into her own register, flat and quick. Shot 2 (l04): Aditya single, on the almirah side, lamp key light, very still. Shot 3 (l05): Kiran close; she gives the name after a breath. Shot 3b (l06): Aditya close, holding on her while she goes straight to business off his face: for the first time he owes her something. Shot 4 (l29), the silent-after frame: Kiran close; she says l29 on it, then waits for his answer through the hold. Her left forearm stays under the pallu throughout.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [sharply] The other code, and two boys would be on those stairs now.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] Then why didn't you say it?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [sighs] Mohit. [quietly] After what happened to him, I couldn't set the boys on you.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] But Mausi only meets a man she can use. So you go in as a thief who married a thief.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Brass set, rented house. Mausi will believe you.

beats.action: She has changed off screen behind the almirah door; there is no changing shot. Shot 1 (l07): Kiran in the grey salwar-kurta beside the open grey-green almirah door, the red saree folded over the wooden chair by the maroon bag, the steel mathri dabba back in the bag's side zip pocket, its lid showing; her RIGHT hand rests on her LEFT cuff, the whole cuff below the sleeve, a hand's width of bare forearm above it. Shot 2 (l08): Aditya single, glasses, key, the red velvet box from the almirah in his left hand. Silent after, two inserts: (1) his long fingers fold the half-empty paper fold shut over the steel tray and take the creased photograph from the sheet and slide both into his right kurta pocket, the print's white edge showing; (2) the brass key, still on its red thread running up out of frame to his neck, turned in the brass padlock on the inside hasp, the shackle open. Padlock clack (sound).

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] I always take the chooda, these wedding bangles, off in the car.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] Leave it on. We arrive as bride and groom.

beats.action: 3:00 (overlay). Silent before: from behind Billu's head and shoulders in the open iron-sheet front door, sodium light at his back, looking up the narrow stairs under the bare yellow bulb: Kiran coming down first in grey, Aditya a step above her, awake. Shot 2 (l09): Billu single, toothpick, eyes wide. Shot 3 (l10): two-shot on the stairs, Kiran in front speaking, Aditya behind her with his eyes on the back of her head: he has just heard her working name. Shot 4 (l11): insert, his hands open the red velvet box, the necklace set inside. Shot 5 (l12): Billu single, laughing once in spite of himself.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [sharply] Kiran? This one's awake, he—

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] He's coming with us. He wants a deal with Mausi.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [chuckles] It's only brass, saale sahab, my wife's brother.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [laughs] Arre, Jijaji! For my sister's husband, even brass will do.

beats.action: Dawn. Silent before: wide exterior, the old white sedan alone on an empty two-lane highway through flat fields, ground mist, blue-grey light; no face readable. Fixed seating: Billu drives front right, Kiran front left, Aditya in the back behind Kiran. Shot 2 (l13): the rear-view mirror with Billu's eyes, toothpick at the corner of the frame, lemon-and-chilli charm hanging below; he does not turn round. Shot 3 (l14): Aditya in the back seat, glasses, key, the faint smile of a greedy man; Billu's eyes in the mirror at frame edge. Shot 3b (l15): Kiran in profile in the front seat, eyes on the road, giving nothing away while he sells the lie she set up. Shot 4 (l16): Billu's LEFT hand holds his phone out on speaker over the gear lever toward Kiran, the marigold string on the dashboard behind it; Kiran in profile. He keeps holding it there through l19. Shot 5 (l17): Kiran single, close, Billu's phone held near her face at frame edge, 'Mausi' overlay on its screen ('मौसी' in the Hindi cut). Shot 5b (l18): from the back seat, Kiran in profile leaning to the phone in Billu's left hand, Aditya's shoulder and glasses soft in the foreground. Shot 6 (l19): insert of the phone in Billu's left hand over the gear lever, the light going orange.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [chuckles] So Jijaji wants to meet Mausi? Mausi meets no one.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] She will. Any pharmacist can taste what's in your sachets.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [chuckles] I run a medical store. The right dose, for a share.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [calm] Told Mausi that Jijaji was awake. Now she wants to hear from you.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Damaad ji was awake, and you told me he drank it?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] If the boys came up, the deal was dead, Mausi.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [quietly] Hmm... bring him, beta.

beats.action: No line. Two set-ups. (1) Insert: Kiran's LEFT hand loose in her lap on the grey kurta, eyes shut or pretending, the first red sun coming through the chooda; the full cuff covers the forearm. (2) From the back seat: in the foreground, soft, Aditya's long fingers sliding the creased print back into his right kurta pocket, its white edge the brightest thing in frame; in the background, sharp, Billu's eyes in the rear-view mirror following that edge into the pocket.

The car stopped at a grey roll-down steel shutter in low orange sun. Shot 1 (l20): exterior two-shot, Aditya at the open front-left door taking Kiran's LEFT hand, the bangle hand, to help her out, playing the husband for Billu; he uses her working name. Silent after, two set-ups: (1) insert, 2 s: his fingers closed over her cuff, the stack shifted a little under them, no skin showing above or below it; late in the set-up the shutter starts to rattle up (sound). (2) Reverse, low from the car door, 2.5 s: the shutter risen, Shakun Mausi standing in it, green saree, keys at her left hip, paan smile; in the soft foreground the two hands are apart: he has looked up and let go. Glimpse A ends on set-up (1), cut before the rattle starts, and must not use set-up (2).

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] Watch your step, Kiran.

beats.action: The bureau's front room, shutter up, no customers: pink walls, daylight from the front, tube light on; Mausi's wooden desk at the back with the grey steel cashbox on it; the low cot along the right wall. Two faces per frame at most. Shot 1 (l21): two-shot, Mausi holding Kiran's face in both hands, Kiran first, her eyes dropping from Mausi's; Mausi's forearms are in frame, bare and unmarked under the green glass bangles. Shot 2 (l22): Mausi single at her desk, the red velvet box open in front of her (Billu's hand at frame edge setting it down, no face), laughing till she coughs. Shot 3 (l23): Chhoti single on the cot, pink phone in her right hand, LEFT hand held out flat, back up, fingertips dipped, the outer forearm bare and unmarked. Shot 4 (l24): Aditya close, his eyes going from one wrist to the other. Shot 5 (l25): Kiran and Aditya side by side near the shutter, his head turned to her, hers not to him.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [sighs] There you are, meri bachchi. Did you eat the mathri?

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [laughs] Brass! Damaad ji turned out to be in our line.

lines.speaker: chhoti
lines.text: [excited] Didi! Look, one hand's ready.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [whispers] Where is Rekha, the one with the burnt wrist?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Not now.

beats.action: Shot 1 (l26): Mausi single at her desk, to Aditya, all business and all warmth. Shot 2 (l27): two-shot, Mausi and Kiran standing at the desk. Shot 3 (l28): insert, Mausi's hand with its green bangles closing on Kiran's LEFT wrist (picture-right) and starting the first ivory bangle of the cuff toward her hennaed knuckles. Silent after, one held set-up: in the soft foreground the two women's hands, the first ivory bangle at Kiran's knuckles; behind them, sharp, Aditya an arm's length away, glasses and key, his eyes on the hands. Focus pull from the hands to his eyes as the camera move. Cut on a glass-bangle chink. Chhoti stays out of these frames.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] You make the sachet, Damaad ji. It's Chhoti's first wedding.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] And you take the chooda off, beta. Tomorrow it goes on Chhoti.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [chuckles] Who buys a new set for every wedding?

sfx_notes: Bedroom bed (b1, b3, b5): a warm still night through the open window, crickets, one distant dog, the lamp's faint electrical hum. No ceiling-fan sound anywhere in this series' bedroom.
b1: Mausi through the phone speaker: light filter only, warm and fully clear; the bed ducks under l02. Call-ended tone, then Aditya's out-breath, close and dry.
b2: sodium-lamp buzz; motorbike engine kicks, revs once and recedes down the lane.
b5: paper crackle as the fold is pressed shut; cloth of the kurta pocket; brass padlock clack and the iron bolt drawn back.
b6: stairwell echo, bare-bulb hum; the iron-sheet front door creaks on its hinge before l09; velvet box hinge snap under l11.

b7 and b8: old sedan engine at steady highway speed, tyre hiss, open-window wind low; birds coming up in the fields. Mausi on Billu's phone speaker (l17, l19): light filter, fully voiced; duck the engine bed under l17 to l19.
b9: engine idling then off, car door clunk, then the steel shutter rattling up, loud and long, starting late in the hand insert and finishing on Mausi. Glimpse A cuts before the rattle starts.

b10 and b11: tube-light hum, a street waking far outside, Mausi's keys chinking at her hip as she moves, glass bangles. Mausi's laugh in l22 breaks into a short paan-smoker's cough. Keys and bangles still under l24 and l25; the whisper dry and close. Duck everything under l27 and l28 so the chooda line is fully clear. The episode cuts on one dry glass-bangle chink, with nothing under it.
music_note: No music under the 2 am call in b1. A single low string drone enters on 'Mohit' (l05) and holds under the rest of the bedroom. The road (b7 to b8) gets a slow plucked pulse over the drone, warm as the light turns orange; it stops dead with the shutter rattle in b9. Bureau: the drone only, very low, rising a little under l27 and l28 and cut hard on the final bangle chink. Instrumental, no melody line, no percussion hits.
ending_question: The chooda is coming off in front of Aditya: will he see the scar on Kiran's wrist, and if he does, what will he do?
writer_notes: S5 English adaptation of content/series1/episodes/s1a01/script.hi.json, not a literal translation. Sources: content/series1/bible.json revision 2 (voice_note_en per character; register.english_version; choice.A.spoken.en; episode title en) and docs/decisions.md D-003, D-005 (direction 7: the code must still sound like a mother's check-in), D-007, D-008, D-013, D-014. Same beat ids (b4 is a gap, as in the Hindi), same line ids l01 to l29 (l29 added inside b3 in the D-024 clarity pass, as in the Hindi), same speakers and order, same tags in the same positions. action, on_screen, location, silent_seconds, silent_position and sfx_notes match the Hindi (b3's action carries the Hindi's clarity-pass note on l29): picture and sound are shared between the two cuts. The one exception is the caller-name overlay text in b1 shot 2 and b7 shot 5, which reads 'Mausi' here (overlays are added in assembly, not in the frames). music_note only swaps the cue word to 'Mohit'.

Locked lines: l01 is the bible's English for choice A, verbatim: 'Yes, Mausi. He drank it.' l13 (Billu's locked line) ends on 'Mausi meets no one.', the episode's English title, with 'So' added as Billu's lead-in. l17 echoes l01 ('you told me he drank it') so Mausi's check lands on Kiran's own words, as 'पी लिया बोला' does in the Hindi.

One word per object (bible register.one_word_per_object): 'sachet' for पुड़िया (l14 'sachets', l26), 'chooda' kept (l07, l27), 'code' (l03), 'deal' in both l10 and l18 for deal and सौदा, so l18 pays off l10 in one word. 'brass' for पीतल in l29, l11 and l22; 'rented' in l29 as in s1e01 l05 ('The set is brass. The house is rented by the month.'). 'set' kept in l28. 'line' kept in l22 as Mausi's trade word ('in our line').

Kept as spoken in Indian English: Mausi, beta, meri bachchi, Damaad ji, Jijaji, saale sahab, Didi, chooda, mathri, arre. Pronunciation dictionary candidates for the English voices: Mausi (MOW-see), beta (BAY-taa), meri bachchi (MAY-ree BUCH-chee), Damaad ji (da-MAAD jee), Jijaji (JEE-jaa-jee), saale sahab (SAA-lay SAA-hab), Didi (DEE-dee), chooda (CHOO-daa), mathri (MUTH-ree), arre (uh-RAY), Kiran (KI-run), Aditya (AA-dit-ya), Billu (BIL-loo), Mohit (MO-hit), Chhoti (CHHO-tee), Rekha (RAY-khaa).

Register: Kiran short and blunt with contractions to Aditya, softer and ending on 'Mausi' with Mausi (the English cannot carry तुम/आप). Aditya in complete sentences, precise nouns, no slang ('Where is Rekha, the one with the burnt wrist?' not 'Where's'). Mausi in short plain sentences with an endearment in every second line (l02, l17, l19, l21, l22, l26, l27). Billu slangier ('This one's awake', 'Arre, Jijaji!'). Chhoti light and quick.

Story locks held: no line says how tight a chooda is, how hard it is to remove or how long it is worn. l07 'I always take ... off in the car' carries the Hindi habitual 'उतार देती हूँ' (her routine, which Aditya then overrules); its gloss 'these wedding bangles' says what the chooda is and nothing about fit, removal or wear time. Aditya first hears 'Kiran' from Billu at l09 and says it himself at l20. Mausi never says Kiran's name. l28 is a rhetorical question about the set and does not touch the ending question.

l09 is a cut-off on a full word ('he—'); l10 cuts straight in with no gap. l06 'So you go in as a thief who married a thief' is Kiran setting the cover story as an instruction, not an accusation; 'But' joins it to l05 as 'पर' does in the Hindi. l11 adds 'only' so a cold viewer hears that the necklace is worthless. C1 round (26 Nov): l11 adds 'my wife's brother' and l12 adds 'For my sister's husband, even brass will do', so the two kinship terms gloss each other inside the joke (see clarity_pass.fixes).

D-014: l19 keeps the pause on the ellipsis after 'Hmm'; the subtitle splits there if the take's pause is 300 ms or longer. Take check: 'Hmm' may garble on v4. If it does, use the fallback '[quietly] All right... bring him, beta.' (same tag, same target).

Tags: all kept from the Hindi, all from the proof-tested group ([calm] [quietly] [sharply] [sighs] [chuckles] [laughs] [excited] [whispers]); none from the verify group. One true whisper (l24). The cliffhanger l27 is [calm], fully voiced, with the bed ducked under it (sfx_notes). Short turns that may need extra takes: l25 'Not now.' (l12 is no longer a short turn after the C1 round). Clarity pass: l05 carries two tags as in the Hindi, [sighs] on the name and [quietly] on the reason, so the name still comes after a breath and the reason stays voiced; l16 moves from [quietly] to [calm] as in the Hindi, because Billu's [quietly] takes measured whispered in the voice review (en l16 included). l24 stays the one true whisper.

Length (D-024 ruling 4; the character measure is withdrawn; hand counts, not measured): about 1,296 dialogue characters with tags removed (about 1,080 before the clarity pass plus 216 net added). Not padded. Line targets against the Hindi: within 15 per cent except l07 (5.0 against 3.4 s: the English-only chooda gloss, allowed by D-024) and l24 (3.8 against 2.8 s: 'the one with the burnt wrist' is the natural English carrier for 'जली कलाई वाली' and echoes s1e02's 'The one with the burnt wrist?'). Still short of the Hindi: l25 (1.2 against 1.4 s), l13 (4.3 against 4.8 s) and l20 (1.8 against 2.0 s).
